text:
Eighteen pine martens now roam the Wyrmwood reserve, the first of the species returned to the site.

The Wyrmwood Reserve Trust released 11 females and 7 males across three sites on 14 October 2023. Dr. Elspeth Harrowgate, the Trust's Lead Conservation Biologist, oversaw the release.

The programme follows the Wyrmwood Reintroduction Feasibility Report (2022), which the Trust's Board of Governors approved before work began.

The 11-to-7 female-to-male split favours breeding potential, and spreading the animals over three sites avoids concentrating the whole founding group in one place.

What it means for the sector: reintroductions of this kind rest on documented feasibility work and board sign-off. Funders and partner organisations are likely to expect the same paper trail, so reserves weighing similar projects should budget for the assessment stage as well as the release itself.
